title: Retrospective conditional hydraulic velocity transfer audit
status_at_write: Written before first prediction scores, after source observations and algebraic head audit were already inspected; not blinded or externally timestamped preregistration
target: Printed measured P5-to-P3 salt-tracer mean velocity in m/s, rounded to 0.001 m/s in author notebook cell87
input_rule: Impose original same-date bed-elevation observations and nearest same-date independent manual station depths. July11 P5 0.8m is author-deduced rather than directly observed. July31 P3 0.38m comes from pressure sensor. No discharge or target velocity enters hydraulic diameter.
velocity_model: v=sqrt(2*g*D*head/(f*L)); g=9.81. Refuse nonpositive head or inputs; no clipping to favorable values.
fit: For each width and head expression, fit one positive amplitude a=1/sqrt(f) by equal-weight training squared error in velocity. Closed form a=sum(x_i*v_i)/sum(x_i^2), x_i=sqrt(2*g*D_i*head_i/L). No test target participates.
metrics: paired MAE reduction of piezometric fitted versus archived-plus fitted
decision: Report every model and width. Superiority across the tested widths requires lower MAE and RMSE than archived-plus fitted at every width, plus lower absolute error on each of four test experiments. Otherwise no consistent-superiority conclusion. This rule is descriptive for this retrospective small sample, not a statistical significance rule.
uncertainty: No confidence interval from four dependent cases. Original floor errors ~0.1m each and depth errors ~0.05m each; corrected late-July heads are comparable to these uncertainties. Width variation alone is not full uncertainty propagation.
scope: Conditional quasi-steady hydraulic hindcast at one channel segment, with externally supplied observed/deduced head and depth. No contact prediction, melt accuracy, discharge forecast, glacier transfer, full coupled model validation, or causal accuracy claim.
preserve: Do not modify author products, original field benchmarks or solver worktree. Save protocol SHA256 with results. Do not tune split, matching, width, objective, or coefficients after scores. Failed outcomes remain reported.
